public_health_question.v: What were the characteristics and clinical course of an unusually large cluster of parechovirus CNS infections in young infants at a Tennessee children’s hospital?

ev.q: An assessment of cases was conducted to better understand this unusually large cluster of infections.

equity.level_reason: Age defines the population (infants aged 5 days–3 months) and sex appears only as a Table descriptor; no other SPD and no equity framing.

ev.q: 23 previously healthy infants aged 5 days–3 months were admitted to a Tennessee children’s hospital
13 (57%) were female and 10 (43%) were male

notes: Mostly a descriptive case series of 23 infants; data_focus is yes because the report compares its own annual case counts (2018, 2019–2021, 2022) at the hospital. The single mean hospital stay is descriptive and does not add a continuous outcome. Social isolation is offered to explain the overall trend, not a social-position difference, so it is not a determinant.
view_issues: Text says 'multiple molecular panel' where 'multiplex' is meant; 2018 count covers only 5 months, so year counts are not on equal periods.
